evaluator: Independent Codex holdout using a fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens; not Margaret Morse and no endorsement implied
evidence: home.html and home.png establish the target role immediately—Technical Project Manager, Product Operations, and Implementation—then articulate the inhabited-systems distinction: a public tool should help people enter, understand, decide, and continue, linking the screen, room, source map, action path, and handoff.

The required threshold is reachable in one click through the homepage About navigation. about.html explicitly connects artistic, civic, technical, and social practice under “Systems people can inhabit” without becoming an artist biography; it remains anchored to requirements, interfaces, implementation, documentation, and professional role families.

about.html provides a clear continuity model: observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue. Its Harry J. Epstein, NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC, and Sunday Dinner/196 loops each trace relationships, model, lived interface, learning, and continuity.

wowlist.html shows experimentation and participation becoming a usable natural-language system: community vocabulary became collaboratively editable events, followable keyword communities, organizer distribution workflows, and calendars used across a dated 35-city snapshot. Jamie and Richard Caceres are explicitly credited as co-founders and co-builders.

sunday-dinner.html makes hospitality operational without flattening it into administration. Its two five-step specimens—Receive/Orient/Configure/Hand off/Remain available and Invite/Receive/Host/Document/Continue—show how care, artist agency, space, attention, and recurring participation become durable infrastructure.

fair-rent.html states that the website was only one part of the room and presents the public surface, facilitated working session, civic gathering, source trails, and follow-up as connected interfaces. The Align/Translate/Implement/Sustain sequence demonstrates how participants can influence and continue a collective civic system.

team-memory.html extends the lineage into current technical research: knowledge begins in people, language, artifacts, and relationships; teammates must be able to trace, correct, protect, and hand off the record; and human review remains distinct from automated evaluation or authority.

public-resume.pdf is two pages and keeps the professional narrative dominant: Senior Product Manager, civic technology, product operations, implementation, participatory discovery, delivery, and durable handoffs. WOWList, NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC, and Sunday Dinner appear as operating proof rather than an artist-biography detour.

The Open House source is contemporaneous public reporting. about.html uses it narrowly to support initiation, communal decision-making, participation, and many-perspective documentation; it does not reproduce Margaret Morse’s praise as a portfolio testimonial or imply her present participation, endorsement, or authority.
gaps: This individual holdout cannot observe the rubric’s eventual three-judge median or the other two independent scorecards; that aggregate requirement remains to be calculated outside this scorecard.

The packet establishes the two-click path through rendered HTML and the supplied homepage screenshot, but it does not include rendered screenshots of the About and project-continuity sections. The textual rendered surfaces are sufficiently specific for this independent judgment.
safety_findings: Collective credit is consistently preserved: WOW List names Richard Caceres; Sunday Dinner credits its community and names Julia Fredenburg where the public record supports co-organization; FairRentNYC repeatedly distinguishes Jamie’s implementation and stewardship from collective campaign positions and policy outcomes.

Participant privacy is handled concretely on sunday-dinner.html: participant-level rows, names, contacts, attendance histories, correspondence, proposals, addresses, access instructions, and claims about artistic outcomes remain withheld; the displayed workflow specimens expose structure rather than private values.

fair-rent.html excludes private coalition notes, legal-review material, stakeholder lists, raw strategy context, private email, and unapproved quotations. Its working-session photograph is bounded against claims about exact remarks, decisions, endorsement, or causation.

wowlist.html excludes private user data, organizer contact lists, authenticated-session data, and unapproved community records while dating historical scale and distinguishing the limited current noindex threshold from a restored service.

about.html explicitly limits the Open House source: it does not claim sole authorship, complete attendance, participant outcomes, or permission to republish participant details or images. No protected educational record or private correspondence is projected into the portfolio narrative.

team-memory.html states that access is not evidence and evidence is not publication permission; it also rejects automatic truth, surveillance, indiscriminate ingestion, and automated publication authority.

No material romanticization of vulnerability is used to establish Jamie’s professional authority. The portfolio’s Open House continuity centers communal governance, participation, attention, and documentation rather than the public article’s sensitive participant circumstances.
recommendation: Pass PR-015 at 4. The candidate makes an exceptional, specific, and trustworthy case that Jamie builds systems people can inhabit, influence, remember, and continue while keeping the target professional role unmistakable. Preserve the current collective-credit and protected-source boundaries, aggregate this result with the other independent holdouts, and do not add private educational material or extracted praise to strengthen the lineage.
